newsitem.title: UK: Dollar supports soft oils in Europe, palm oil lower.
newsitem.headline: Dollar supports soft oils in Europe, palm oil lower.

text.p: A slightly stronger dollar against European currencies on Friday afternoon offset lower Chicago futures in the soft oil sector.
Chicago soy futures fell on talk that China had cancelled soymeal purchases of around 400,000 tonnes from South America and 20,000 tonnes from India.
However, the slightly firmer dollar offset the impact of Chicago and European soft oils closed unchanged from midday with soy and rape oil 1.50 guilders up.

Palm oil prices drifted off from their midday levels but higher prices in the Far East ahead of the Malaysian Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's(PORLA) export, output and stocks data for January due out on Saturday put a floor under the market.
The PORLA data was delayed by one week due to the recent long holiday in Malaysia.
Palm oil prices rose in Malaysia because local players believe the PORLA data will be friendly to the market.
Crude palm oil cif Europe closed $2.50 up to unchanged after Apr/Jun traded at $567.50 a tonne cif.
Products were $5 higher with no further business reported.
Coconut oil close mixed with sellers $2.50 up to $5 down while palmkernel oil was $2.50 lower in tradeless markets.
Dutch soy oil traded at 101.25 guilders for Apr, 102 for May and 103 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill for Aug/Sep, but traders said the volume was modest.
